user.title: Set up Vome
user.description:
Vome uses **keypair authentication** with a locally stored signing key.

Use **Generate new user key** to create a fresh signing key, or untick to paste an existing one after submit. After setup, back up the signing key from **More → Backup signing key**.

⚠️ Anyone with the UID can view switch state and activity in Public mode.

subscribe_switch.title: Subscribe to a switch
subscribe_switch.description:
Enter a switch UID, or paste a **uid/key** composite (e.g. `vs_abc123/your-access-key`). The name will be fetched automatically.

Access keys enable toggling. Find public switches at sync.vome.io.

link_vome.title: Connect to Vome Home
link_vome.description:
1. Open **{verification_uri}** and sign in with GitHub.
2. Enter this code: **{user_code}**
3. Come back here and continue.

Your Home Assistant will then appear in your Vome account and can be brokered by the home-assistant-mcp server — no public IP, port-forwarding or Nabu Casa needed.

link_vome_retry.title: Connect to Vome Home
link_vome_retry.description: The Vome portal could not be reached to start the connection. Press **Submit** to try again.

link_vome_confirm.title: Connect to Vome Home
link_vome_confirm.description:
Approve the code **{user_code}** at **{verification_uri}**, then press **Submit**.

Nothing else is needed — the component creates its own local access token (it appears in your profile as “Vome relay”).

link_vome_alt.title: Alternative connection
link_vome_alt.description:
Approve the code **{user_code}** at **{verification_uri}**, then press **Submit**.

Only fill these in if the automatic connection does not work for your setup (custom `server_host`, TLS on the local API, or an ESPHome dashboard that add-on discovery cannot find).

data.local_token: Local long-lived access token (overrides the automatic one)
data.esphome_url: ESPHome dashboard URL (auto-detected on HAOS / Supervised)

unlink_vome.title: Disconnect from Vome Home
unlink_vome.description: This will stop the relay and remove this Home Assistant from your Vome account's relay access.

relay_server.title: Advanced: relay server URL
relay_server.description: Overrides the WebSocket URL this Home Assistant dials out to (normally set once when you connect to Vome). Only change this if you know what you're doing — e.g. testing against a non-production relay. Leave blank to reset to the default (`{default_url}`).

remote_access.title: Remote access & LAN tunnels
remote_access.description:
With an active friendly domain on vome.io, traffic reaches this home over the outbound relay (no router port-forward).

**Allow full-UI forwarding** exposes this Home Assistant at your friendly domain. Keep it off unless you need browser access to HA itself.

**LAN tunnels** map `https://your-domain/t/<slug>/` to a device on your network (NAS, router, printer UI, Guacamole, …). You currently have **{lan_enabled}** of **{lan_count}** route(s) enabled.
